reading.title: People Strategy 2027-2029: context and priorities
paragraphs: Corvane Logistics France - People Strategy 2027-2029 (extract)
1. Strategic context

The Group's business plan assumes a 30% increase in volumes in France over three years, driven largely by two new automated warehouses. Delivering this plan will depend less on capital expenditure than on our ability to attract, retain and develop the right people. At present, our HR priorities have grown up organically, site by site, and are not always aligned with the business strategy.

Three indicators illustrate the challenge. Regretted attrition among maintenance technicians reached 14% over the last twelve months. The absence rate in our warehouses remains well above the industry average. And almost half of our frontline managers have been in post for less than two years, with little formal preparation for the role.
2. Strategic priorities

We therefore propose to concentrate effort and investment on three strategic priorities: (i) securing critical skills, particularly in maintenance and automation; (ii) building manager capability, so that every team leader can set expectations, hold difficult conversations and lead a team through change; and (iii) simplifying our HR operating model, with clearer roles for HR business partners and a single service centre for administrative requests.

Each priority will be underpinned by a small number of measurable targets, reported quarterly in the HR dashboard alongside leading indicators such as engagement and short-term absence. Initiatives that do not contribute to these priorities will be deprioritised or stopped, subject to any legal or contractual commitments already in place.
3. Governance

The HR Director will own the roadmap and report progress to the Management Committee each quarter. Any proposal affecting the organisation of work will be subject to prior information and consultation of the works council, in accordance with applicable law.

They were imposed by the Group

questions.explain_fr: « The HR Director will own the roadmap » : « to own » = en être responsable. Le comité de direction reçoit le reporting.

reading.title: Narrative for the board's HR slide
paragraphs: Board meeting, 14 November - Item 6: People update (speaker notes for slide 3)
This slide summarises our headline HR metrics for the third quarter. Overall, the picture is mixed: retention is improving, but absence and time to hire are moving in the wrong direction.

Voluntary turnover fell to 11.2% on a rolling twelve-month basis, down from 13.5% year on year. Exit interviews suggest that the new career paths for technicians are beginning to have an effect, although it is too early to draw firm conclusions.

The absence rate, on the other hand, rose to 6.1%, against a target of 5%. The increase is concentrated in two warehouses and consists mostly of short, repeated absences. We read this as an early warning sign rather than a medical issue, and the site managers have been asked to hold return-to-work conversations systematically from December.

Time to hire has lengthened to 58 days on average, largely because of the hiring freeze on non-critical roles introduced in July. This was a deliberate trade-off to protect the payroll-to-revenue ratio, which remains within budget at 38%.

The bottom line: we are on track on cost and retention, but we need to keep a close eye on absence. We are not asking the Board for a decision today; this item is for information. A deep dive on absence will be presented at the March meeting, together with a proposal for manager training.

reading.title: A manager escalates a team conflict
paragraphs: Subject: Need your help - situation in the customer service team
Hi Sophie,
I'm sorry to land this on you on a Friday, but I think I need to loop you in on something before it gets worse.

As you know, Léa and Marc have both been on my team for about three years. Since the reorganisation in September, when Léa took over the key accounts that Marc used to handle, there has been a real falling-out between them. They barely speak in meetings, they copy me into every email exchange, and on Tuesday they had a heated argument in the open-plan office in front of the whole team.

I've tried to deal with it informally. I had a quiet word with each of them separately last month, and they both promised to make an effort, but nothing has really changed. Team morale is clearly suffering - two people have told me they dread coming in on the days both are in the office.

To be honest, I'm not sure what my role is here. Part of me thinks they're adults and should sort it out themselves; part of me thinks I should have stepped in much earlier. I also don't want to take sides, because I think they're both partly at fault.

Could we find half an hour early next week? I'd like your advice on what to do next, and whether this is something HR should handle or something I need to deal with myself. I've kept a short paper trail of the incidents, which I can send you beforehand.
Thanks in advance,
Thomas

glossary.plain: inform you and include you in the discussion
a serious disagreement that damages a relationship

how confident and motivated the team feels
become involved to deal with a problem

questions.q: What triggered the conflict between Léa and Marc?
options: A change of responsibilities after the reorganisation

Moved one of them to another team
questions.explain_fr: « I had a quiet word with each of them separately » : entretiens informels individuels.

questions.q: What is Thomas unsure about?
options: What his own role is and whether HR should take over
questions.explain_fr: Il s'interroge sur son rôle et sur la répartition manager/RH : « whether this is something HR should handle ».

questions.q: Which detail shows the conflict affects others?
options: Colleagues dread the days both are in the office
questions.explain_fr: L'impact sur le collectif (« team morale is clearly suffering ») est illustré par les collègues qui redoutent de venir au bureau.

reading.title: Policy: addressing performance concerns informally
paragraphs: Halden Systems France SAS - Manager Guidance No. 4: Addressing Performance Concerns Informally
1. Purpose and scope

1.1 This guidance applies to all people managers of the French entities. It sets out the steps to be taken where an employee's performance falls below the expected standard, before any formal procedure is considered.
1.2 It is intended to support, not to replace, the manager's judgement, and shall be read in conjunction with the internal rules and the applicable collective agreement.
2. Principles
2.1 Managers are expected to address performance issues promptly. Concerns that are left unaddressed for long periods are harder to resolve and may undermine the credibility of any subsequent action.

2.2 The first step shall be an informal discussion in which the manager sets clear expectations, explains the gap between the expected and actual standard, and listens to the employee's explanation. Possible causes outside the employee's control, such as workload, lack of training or health issues, must be explored.

2.3 Following the discussion, the manager should send the employee a short written summary of what was agreed, including any support offered and a date for review. Such a summary does not constitute a disciplinary sanction.
3. Escalation to HR

3.1 Managers shall contact their HR business partner where (a) no improvement is observed by the review date, (b) the employee raises a health, harassment or discrimination concern, or (c) the manager is considering any formal measure.
3.2 Under no circumstances should a manager announce or imply a sanction or dismissal without prior consultation with HR.

glossary.plain: managers who have staff reporting to them
deal directly with problems in how someone is doing their job
explains exactly what is expected and to what standard
a short document recording what was said and agreed
the HR adviser dedicated to a business area
make something less believable or convincing

legalese.phrase: shall be read in conjunction with
does not constitute a disciplinary sanction

questions.q: When does this guidance apply?
options: Before any formal procedure is considered
Only for employees with cadre status
questions.explain_fr: Le texte vise l'étape informelle : « before any formal procedure is considered ».

questions.q: Why should managers act promptly, according to section 2.1?
options: Because the law sets a strict deadline
Because old, unaddressed issues are harder to resolve and weaken later action
questions.explain_fr: Le texte invoque une raison pratique (« harder to resolve ») et de crédibilité (« undermine the credibility of any subsequent action »).

questions.q: What is the status of the written summary sent after the discussion?
options: It is not a disciplinary sanction
It must be signed by HR
questions.explain_fr: « Such a summary does not constitute a disciplinary sanction » : c'est une trace, pas une sanction.

questions.q: In which situation must the manager contact HR?
options: Whenever they hold an informal discussion
When the employee raises a harassment concern
questions.explain_fr: Point 3.1 (b) : un signalement de santé, de harcèlement ou de discrimination impose de solliciter le HRBP.

writing.title: Advising a manager by email on an underperformer
writing.brief: Julien, a sales manager, has asked whether he can 'just put Nadia on a warning' because her results have dropped over the last three months. Reply by email: advise him to start with an informal conversation, tell him what to cover, and offer your help.
writing.brief_fr: Julien, manager commercial, demande s'il peut « simplement donner un avertissement » à Nadia, dont les résultats baissent depuis trois mois. Répondez-lui par e-mail : conseillez-lui de commencer par un échange informel, indiquez-lui quoi aborder et proposez votre aide.

gaps.text: Thanks for ___ this with me before taking any action - that's exactly the right instinct.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To raise something with someone' = soulever un sujet auprès de quelqu'un. On ne dit pas 'to rise this'.

gaps.text: At this stage, I would ___ against a formal warning.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To advise against' = déconseiller. Verbe avec 's' (/z/) ; le nom 'advice' s'écrit avec 'c'.

gaps.text: Nobody has yet told Nadia clearly what is expected of her, so the first step is to ___ expectations.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To set expectations' = fixer des attentes claires. Collocation figée, très fréquente en management.

gaps.text: It is also worth finding out whether something is going on ___ the scenes, such as a workload or health issue.
gaps.explain_fr: 'Behind the scenes' = en coulisses. Toujours avec 'behind', jamais 'behind the scene' au singulier dans ce sens.

gaps.text: After your conversation, please send her a short email summarising what you agreed, so that we have a ___ trail.
gaps.explain_fr: 'Paper trail' = trace écrite, même quand les échanges sont électroniques.

gaps.text: I'd be happy to ___ you through how to structure the conversation before you see her.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To walk someone through' = expliquer pas à pas. 'Talk someone through' et 'take someone through' sont aussi naturels.

writing.model:
Hi Julien,

Thanks for raising this with me before taking any action - that's exactly the right instinct.

At this stage, I would advise against a formal warning. Nobody has yet told Nadia clearly what is expected of her, so the first step is to set expectations. I'd suggest an informal one-to-one this week: share the figures, explain the gap between where she is and where she needs to be, and above all listen to her explanation. It is also worth finding out whether something is going on behind the scenes, such as a workload or health issue.

After your conversation, please send her a short email summarising what you agreed, so that we have a paper trail. Agree a review date in four to six weeks.

I'd be happy to walk you through how to structure the conversation before you see her. Would Wednesday afternoon work?

Best,
Sophie

commentary.quote: that's exactly the right instinct
commentary.note_fr: On valorise la démarche du manager avant de le contredire : il reviendra vers les RH la prochaine fois.

commentary.quote: I would advise against a formal warning
commentary.note_fr: Le conditionnel 'would' adoucit le conseil sans l'affaiblir. Plus naturel que 'you must not'.

commentary.quote: and above all listen to her explanation
commentary.note_fr: 'Above all' met en relief le point clé ; préférable à 'moreover' ou 'indeed'.

commentary.quote: so that we have a paper trail
commentary.note_fr: 'So that' introduit le but de la consigne : on explique pourquoi, le manager adhère mieux.

commentary.quote: Would Wednesday afternoon work?
commentary.note_fr: Proposer un créneau précis transforme l'offre d'aide en action concrète.

checklist: Did I acknowledge the manager's request before redirecting it?
Is my recommendation clear in the first lines?
Did I explain why an informal step comes first?
Did I mention possible causes outside the employee's control?
Did I ask for a written record and a review date?
Did I offer concrete help with a date?
phrasebank: Thanks for raising this with me before taking any action.
At this stage, I would advise against...
The first step is to set clear expectations.
It is also worth finding out whether...
Please send her a short email summarising what you agreed.
I'd be happy to walk you through...
Would Wednesday afternoon work?

writing.title: Minutes: executive committee discussion on HR KPIs
writing.brief: Write the HR item of the minutes of the executive committee of Varuna Technologies France. The committee reviewed the quarterly HR dashboard, discussed the rise in absence, rejected a proposal to lift the hiring freeze and asked HR for a deep dive.
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez le point RH du compte rendu du comité exécutif de Varuna Technologies France. Le comité a examiné le tableau de bord RH trimestriel, discuté de la hausse de l'absentéisme, refusé de lever le gel des recrutements et demandé une analyse approfondie aux RH.

gaps.text: The HR Director ___ the Committee through the HR dashboard for the third quarter.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To take someone through' = présenter en détail. Au passé dans un compte rendu : 'took'.

gaps.text: Voluntary turnover had fallen by 2.3 points year ___ year.
gaps.explain_fr: 'Year on year' (UK) / 'year over year' (US) = en glissement annuel.

gaps.text: Members expressed concern at the rise in the absence ___, which now stands at 6.1%.
gaps.explain_fr: 'Absence rate' = taux d'absentéisme. 'Stands at' = s'établit à, tournure standard pour un indicateur.

gaps.text: The proposal to lift the hiring ___ was not approved.
gaps.explain_fr: 'To lift a hiring freeze' = lever un gel des recrutements.

gaps.text: The Committee asked HR to carry out a deep ___ on absence at the two sites concerned.
gaps.explain_fr: 'A deep dive' = une analyse approfondie. 'To carry out' est le verbe neutre des comptes rendus.

gaps.text: Action: HR to present its findings, ___ with recommendations, at the January meeting.
gaps.explain_fr: 'Together with' = accompagné de. Style télégraphique 'HR to present' typique des actions dans les minutes.

writing.model:
Item 4: HR dashboard - Q3

The HR Director took the Committee through the HR dashboard for the third quarter. Voluntary turnover had fallen by 2.3 points year on year, which she attributed in part to the new career paths for technicians.

Members expressed concern at the rise in the absence rate, which now stands at 6.1%, against a target of 5%. It was noted that the increase was concentrated at the Lyon support centre and the Marseille site.

The proposal to lift the hiring freeze was not approved. The CFO stressed that the payroll-to-revenue ratio should remain within budget until the end of the financial year.

The Committee asked HR to carry out a deep dive on absence at the two sites concerned.

Action: HR to present its findings, together with recommendations, at the January meeting.

commentary.quote: which she attributed in part to
commentary.note_fr: 'To attribute something to' = imputer à. 'In part' nuance l'analyse : on reste prudent sur les causes.

commentary.quote: Members expressed concern at
commentary.note_fr: Formule classique des comptes rendus britanniques ; on rapporte une position collective sans nommer chacun.

commentary.quote: It was noted that
commentary.note_fr: Le passif impersonnel est normal dans des minutes : il consigne un constat sans l'attribuer.

commentary.quote: was not approved
commentary.note_fr: Formulation neutre pour une décision négative ; évitez 'was refused', plus sec.

commentary.quote: Action: HR to present its findings
commentary.note_fr: Infinitif sans auxiliaire pour les actions : bref, clair, avec un responsable et une échéance.

checklist: Is the item clearly numbered and titled?
Did I use the past tense consistently for what was said?
Is each figure given with its comparison or target?
Is the decision stated neutrally and unambiguously?
Does every action have an owner and a deadline?
phrasebank: X took the Committee through...
Members expressed concern at...
It was noted that...
The proposal was not approved.
The Committee asked HR to...
Action: HR to present its findings at the next meeting.
which now stands at...

writing.title: Talking points for a difficult conversation
writing.brief: Camille, a newly promoted team leader, must tell a former peer, Hugo, that his repeated lateness to client calls is no longer acceptable. Write one paragraph of talking points (120-160 words) she can use to open and structure the conversation.
writing.brief_fr: Camille, récemment promue cheffe d'équipe, doit dire à un ancien collègue, Hugo, que ses retards répétés aux appels clients ne sont plus acceptables. Rédigez un paragraphe de points clés (120 à 160 mots) pour ouvrir et structurer l'échange.
outline: Open by naming the purpose of the meeting directly, without small talk
State the facts precisely (dates, calls), not judgements
Explain the impact on clients and the team
Acknowledge the change in your relationship
Ask for his view and listen
Agree what happens next and when you will review it
writing.model: Hugo, I wanted to talk to you about something specific, and I'd rather get straight to the point. You joined the client calls late on three occasions this month: on the 4th, the 11th and the 18th. On the last one, the client asked me whether we were still interested in the account. That puts the relationship at risk, and it means the rest of the team ends up covering for you. I know this is a bit awkward - a few months ago we were working side by side, and now I'm the one raising it. But it's precisely because I value working with you that I'd rather be upfront. Is there something going on that I should know about? I'd like to hear your side. What I need from now on is for you to be on every call on time. Let's check in again in two weeks and see where we are.

commentary.quote: I'd rather get straight to the point
commentary.note_fr: Annoncer qu'on va droit au but évite de 'beat around the bush' et rassure sur la transparence.

commentary.quote: on the 4th, the 11th and the 18th
commentary.note_fr: Des faits datés plutôt qu'un jugement ('you're always late') : l'échange reste factuel et incontestable.

commentary.quote: I know this is a bit awkward
commentary.note_fr: Nommer la gêne liée au changement de statut désamorce la tension. 'A bit' : understatement britannique.

commentary.quote: Is there something going on that I should know about?
commentary.note_fr: Question ouverte qui laisse place à une cause cachée (santé, situation personnelle).

commentary.quote: What I need from now on is
commentary.note_fr: Structure clivée ('What I need is...') : met en relief l'attente sans agressivité.

checklist: Do I state the purpose within the first two sentences?
Are the facts specific and dated?
Did I explain the impact, not just the behaviour?
Did I leave room for his explanation?
Is the expectation clear and measurable?
Is there a follow-up date?
phrasebank: I wanted to talk to you about something specific.
I'd rather get straight to the point.
That puts ... at risk.
I know this is a bit awkward.
I'd like to hear your side.
What I need from now on is...
Let's check in again in two weeks.

writing.title: Commentary on the quarterly HR dashboard
writing.brief: Write the commentary paragraph (120-160 words) that accompanies the quarterly HR dashboard sent to the US parent company. Turnover is down, absence is up, time to hire is longer because of the hiring freeze. Use American spelling.
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez le paragraphe de commentaire (120 à 160 mots) qui accompagne le tableau de bord RH trimestriel envoyé à la maison mère américaine. Le turnover baisse, l'absentéisme augmente, le délai de recrutement s'allonge à cause du gel des embauches. Orthographe américaine.
outline: One-sentence overall message
Turnover: figure, trend, likely reason
Absence: figure versus target, where it is concentrated, what is being done
Time to hire: figure and reason (deliberate trade-off)
What to watch next quarter
writing.model: Overall, Q3 shows progress on retention but a deterioration in absence. Voluntary turnover fell to 11.2% on a rolling 12-month basis, down from 13.5% year over year; exit data suggests that the new technician career paths are starting to pay off. Absence, by contrast, rose to 6.1% against a target of 5%. The increase is concentrated at two sites and consists mainly of short, repeated absences, which we see as an early warning sign of disengagement rather than a medical trend. Site managers will hold systematic return-to-work conversations from December. Time to hire lengthened to 58 days, as expected, because of the hiring freeze on non-critical roles - a deliberate trade-off to keep the payroll ratio within budget. Next quarter, the key metric to watch is short-term absence; we will share a deep dive with the leadership team in January.

commentary.quote: Overall, Q3 shows progress on retention but a deterioration in absence.
commentary.note_fr: Le message principal d'abord ('bottom line up front'), comme l'attend un lecteur américain.

commentary.quote: year over year
commentary.note_fr: Forme américaine, puisque le destinataire est la maison mère aux États-Unis ; en UK : 'year on year'.

commentary.quote: are starting to pay off
commentary.note_fr: 'To pay off' = porter ses fruits. Le verbe 'suggests' qui précède garde la prudence nécessaire.

commentary.quote: by contrast
commentary.note_fr: Connecteur de contraste net et élégant, préférable à 'on the contrary' (qui contredit une affirmation).

commentary.quote: a deliberate trade-off
commentary.note_fr: Présenter un indicateur dégradé comme un arbitrage assumé montre la maîtrise de la situation.

checklist: Does the first sentence give the overall message?
Is every figure compared with a target or a previous period?
Did I explain causes cautiously ('suggests', 'we see this as')?
Did I say what action is being taken?
Did I use American spelling and conventions consistently?
phrasebank: Overall, the quarter shows...
X fell to ... on a rolling 12-month basis.
Y, by contrast, rose to ... against a target of ...
The increase is concentrated at...
as expected, because of...
a deliberate trade-off to...
The key metric to watch next quarter is...

writing.title: Pushing back on a CEO's decision
writing.brief: Martin Hale, the British CEO of the French subsidiary, has decided to announce at next Monday's town hall that the Lyon customer service team will move to Lisbon. No one has informed the works council. Write him an email (200-260 words) supporting the business objective but pushing back firmly on the timing, explaining the risks and proposing an alternative.
writing.brief_fr: Martin Hale, CEO britannique de la filiale française, a décidé d'annoncer lundi prochain en réunion plénière le transfert à Lisbonne de l'équipe service client de Lyon. Le CSE n'a pas été informé. Écrivez-lui un e-mail (200 à 260 mots) qui soutient l'objectif mais conteste fermement le calendrier, expose les risques et propose une alternative.
outline: Acknowledge the business rationale and show you support the objective
State your concern clearly: announcing before consulting the works council
Explain the legal and practical risks without legal jargon
Propose an alternative timetable and what can be said on Monday
Offer to discuss and make clear the decision is his, with your advice on record
writing.model:
Dear Martin,

Thank you for sharing your plans for the customer service team ahead of Monday's town hall. I understand the business case for consolidating the activity in Lisbon, and I'm keen to help you deliver it.

I do, however, have a serious concern about the timing. Under French law, a project of this kind must be put to the works council for information and consultation before any decision is final. If the move is announced on Monday as a done deal, the works council could argue that it has been presented with a fait accompli. That would expose the company to a claim for obstruction, could delay the project by several months and would almost certainly damage trust with the team and its representatives.

I would therefore suggest a slightly different sequence. On Monday, you could explain that the company is reviewing the organisation of customer service and that a proposal will be submitted to the works council shortly. We would then table the project at an extraordinary works council meeting within the next two to three weeks, with a clear timetable and the support measures we intend to offer.

This would cost us a few weeks at the start, but it would protect the project as a whole.

I'd welcome the chance to talk this through with you before Monday - perhaps tomorrow morning? Ultimately the decision is yours, but I wanted to set out my advice clearly.

Kind regards,

Sophie

commentary.quote: I'm keen to help you deliver it
commentary.note_fr: On se place du côté de l'objectif avant de contester la méthode : la critique porte sur le 'comment', pas sur le 'quoi'.

commentary.quote: I do, however, have a serious concern about the timing.
commentary.note_fr: Le 'do' d'insistance et 'however' en incise marquent le désaccord avec fermeté mais sans agressivité.

commentary.quote: as a done deal
commentary.note_fr: 'A done deal' = une affaire conclue. L'expression française 'fait accompli' est aussi employée en anglais.

commentary.quote: That would expose the company to a claim for obstruction
commentary.note_fr: Le délit d'entrave rendu par 'obstruction', avec les conséquences concrètes qui parlent à un dirigeant : délai, confiance.

commentary.quote: I would therefore suggest a slightly different sequence.
commentary.note_fr: 'Slightly' minimise l'écart proposé : understatement britannique qui facilite l'acceptation.

commentary.quote: Ultimately the decision is yours, but I wanted to set out my advice clearly.
commentary.note_fr: On respecte l'autorité du CEO tout en laissant une trace claire du conseil donné.

checklist: Did I show support for the business objective before raising my concern?
Is the concern stated clearly in one sentence?
Did I explain the risks in business terms (cost, delay, trust)?
Did I offer a workable alternative, including what can be said now?
Did I respect his authority while putting my advice on record?
Is the tone firm but courteous throughout?
phrasebank: I understand the business case for...
I do, however, have a serious concern about...
Under French law, a project of this kind must...
That would expose the company to...
I would therefore suggest a slightly different sequence.
This would cost us a few weeks, but it would protect...
Ultimately the decision is yours, but I wanted to set out my advice clearly.

writing.title: Executive summary of HR priorities
writing.brief: Write the executive summary (200-260 words) of the HR roadmap for 2027 that you will present to the board of Corvane Logistics France. Give the context, three priorities with one target each, the budget requested and the decision expected from the board.
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez la synthèse (200 à 260 mots) de la feuille de route RH 2027 que vous présenterez au conseil de Corvane Logistics France : contexte, trois priorités avec un objectif chacune, budget demandé et décision attendue du conseil.
outline: The decision requested from the board, up front
Business context and why HR matters to it
Three priorities, each with one measurable target
Budget and how it is funded
Main risk and how it will be managed
writing.model:
Executive summary

The Board is invited to approve the 2027 HR roadmap and an associated budget of EUR 620,000.

Our business plan relies on opening two automated warehouses and growing volumes by 30% over three years. The main constraint is no longer equipment but people: we are losing skilled technicians, absence is above the industry average and many of our frontline managers have had little preparation for the role. The roadmap therefore focuses on three priorities.

First, securing critical skills: we aim to bring regretted attrition among maintenance technicians down from 14% to below 9% by the end of 2027. Second, building manager capability: every team leader will complete a six-module programme covering difficult conversations, change and the basics of French labour law. Third, simplifying the HR operating model, so that HR business partners spend at least half their time advising managers rather than processing requests.

The budget will be largely funded by savings on agency fees and recruitment costs. Progress will be reported quarterly in the HR dashboard.

The main risk lies in implementation: the programme will only succeed if site directors free up their managers' time. We will mitigate this by agreeing training slots with each site in advance and by including manager capability in directors' objectives.
writing.model_us:
Executive summary

The Board is asked to approve the 2027 HR roadmap and an associated budget of EUR 620,000.

Our business plan relies on opening two automated warehouses and growing volumes by 30% over three years. The main constraint is no longer equipment but people: we are losing skilled technicians, absenteeism is above the industry average, and many of our frontline managers have had little preparation for the role. The roadmap therefore focuses on three priorities.

First, securing critical skills: we aim to bring regretted attrition among maintenance technicians down from 14% to below 9% by year-end 2027. Second, building manager capability: every team leader will complete a six-module program covering difficult conversations, change, and the basics of French labor law. Third, simplifying the HR operating model, so that HR business partners spend at least half their time advising managers rather than processing requests.

The budget will be funded largely by savings on agency fees and recruiting costs. We will report progress quarterly in the HR dashboard.

The main risk is execution: the program will only succeed if site directors free up their managers' time. We will mitigate this by locking in training slots with each site in advance and by building manager capability into directors' goals.

commentary.quote: The Board is invited to approve
commentary.note_fr: Formule britannique standard des documents de conseil : la décision attendue figure dès la première ligne. En US : 'is asked to approve'.

commentary.quote: The main constraint is no longer equipment but people
commentary.note_fr: Structure 'no longer X but Y' : elle relie l'enjeu RH à la stratégie de l'entreprise en une phrase.

commentary.quote: First, securing critical skills
commentary.note_fr: 'First, Second, Third' structurent la synthèse ; évitez 'Firstly... Secondly', plus lourds.

commentary.quote: from 14% to below 9% by the end of 2027
commentary.note_fr: Chaque priorité est assortie d'un objectif chiffré et daté : c'est ce que le conseil retiendra.

commentary.quote: We will mitigate this by
commentary.note_fr: 'To mitigate' = atténuer. Un risque n'est crédible que s'il est accompagné de sa parade.

checklist: Is the decision requested stated in the first sentence?
Is the link between HR and the business strategy explicit?
Does each priority have a measurable target?
Did I say how the budget is funded?
Did I name the main risk and how it will be managed?
Is it under 260 words?
phrasebank: The Board is invited to approve...
Our business plan relies on...
The roadmap therefore focuses on three priorities.
We aim to bring X down from ... to ... by ...
The budget will be largely funded by...
Progress will be reported quarterly in...
The main risk lies in... We will mitigate this by...

dialogues.title: Coaching a newly promoted manager
dialogues.context: Sophie, HR Director of the French subsidiary of a British group, meets Oliver, who was promoted a month ago to lead the team he used to work in. He is struggling to delegate and to manage his former peers.
dialogues.context_fr: Sophie, DRH de la filiale française d'un groupe britannique, rencontre Oliver, promu il y a un mois à la tête de l'équipe dont il faisait partie. Il a du mal à déléguer et à manager ses anciens collègues.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: So, a month in. How are you finding it, honestly?
lines.note_fr: 'How are you finding it?' = comment ça se passe pour vous ? Tournure britannique très naturelle pour demander un ressenti.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Honestly? Exhausting. I'm doing my old job and the new one, and I'm working until nine most nights.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: That's quite common in the first few months. Can I ask what you're still doing yourself that someone in the team could pick up?
lines.note_fr: Question ouverte de coaching : on aide le manager à trouver lui-même la réponse. 'To pick up' = reprendre une tâche.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Well, the monthly reporting, for a start. But it's quicker if I do it. If I hand it over to Priya, I'll only end up checking every line.
lines.note_fr: 'For a start' = pour commencer. 'To hand over' = confier, transmettre.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Quicker this month, perhaps. But in six months you'll still be doing it, and Priya won't have learnt anything. Delegating takes longer at first - that's the investment.
lines.note_fr: 'Learnt' (UK) / 'learned' (US). L'argument met en balance court terme et long terme.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Fair enough. The harder bit, to be honest, is Hugo. We used to go for drinks every Friday, and now I'm meant to tell him his work isn't up to scratch.
lines.note_fr: 'Up to scratch' = au niveau attendu. 'I'm meant to' = je suis censé (UK) ; en US, plutôt 'I'm supposed to'.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: That's probably the hardest part of the transition. What do you think he expects from you now?

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: I suspect he expects me to let things slide. And I have, a bit.
lines.note_fr: 'To let things slide' = laisser couler, ne pas réagir.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Then I'd suggest you have a quiet word with him this week. Acknowledge that it's a bit odd for both of you, then be very clear about what you need from him. You don't have to stop being friendly - you just can't stop being his manager.
lines.note_fr: 'A quiet word' : entretien discret et informel, expression typiquement britannique.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: And if he takes it badly?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Then he takes it badly, and you deal with that. But in my experience, people respect a manager who's straight with them far more than one who beats around the bush.
lines.note_fr: 'Straight with someone' = franc, honnête. 'To beat around the bush' = tourner autour du pot.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Right. Could we go through how I'd open the conversation? I'd rather not wing it.
lines.note_fr: 'To wing it' = improviser sans préparation (familier).

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Of course. Let's do that now, and we'll check in again in a fortnight to see how the reporting's going with Priya.
lines.note_fr: 'A fortnight' = quinze jours, très britannique ; les Américains disent 'two weeks'.

questions.q: Why does Oliver resist delegating the monthly reporting?
options: He thinks it is faster to do it himself
His boss has asked him to keep it
questions.explain_fr: « It's quicker if I do it » : l'argument classique du manager qui ne délègue pas.

questions.q: What does Sophie advise about Hugo?
options: To move Hugo to another team
To talk to him privately and be clear about expectations
To wait for the annual review
questions.explain_fr: Elle conseille « a quiet word » et d'être « very clear about what you need from him ».

questions.q: What will happen in two weeks?
options: They will meet again to review progress
Oliver will start a formal procedure
Hugo will be given a warning
questions.explain_fr: « We'll check in again in a fortnight » : un point de suivi dans quinze jours.

dialogues.title: Executive committee: what the HR numbers really say
dialogues.context: Executive committee of Corvane Logistics France. Martin, the CEO, Fiona, the CFO, and Sophie, HR Director, discuss the quarterly HR dashboard.
dialogues.context_fr: Comité exécutif de Corvane Logistics France. Martin (CEO), Fiona (directrice financière) et Sophie (DRH) commentent le tableau de bord RH trimestriel.

lines.speaker: Martin
lines.text: Right, item four. Sophie, the people numbers. Keep it brief if you can - we're running late.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Of course. Three things to take away. Turnover is down two points on last year, absence is up, and time to hire has gone out to almost sixty days.
lines.note_fr: 'Three things to take away' : on annonce le plan d'emblée. 'Down two points on last year' = en baisse de deux points sur un an.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: The time to hire doesn't worry me. That's the freeze doing what it's supposed to do.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Agreed, that one's a deliberate trade-off. Absence is what I'd like us to focus on. It's six point one per cent against a target of five, and it's almost entirely in two warehouses.
lines.note_fr: 'Six point one per cent' : on lit la décimale avec 'point'. 'Against a target of' = pour un objectif de.

lines.speaker: Martin
lines.text: Isn't that just the winter flu season?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: That was my first thought too, but it doesn't quite fit. It's short absences, mostly Mondays, and it started in September - well before flu season. It tends to be a leading indicator of disengagement rather than illness.
lines.note_fr: 'It doesn't quite fit' = ça ne colle pas tout à fait : désaccord adouci. 'Leading indicator' = indicateur avancé.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: What's it costing us?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Roughly the equivalent of twelve full-time posts in temporary cover. So it's not trivial.
lines.note_fr: 'Not trivial' : understatement britannique pour dire que c'est significatif.

lines.speaker: Martin
lines.text: And what's driving it? Do we know?
lines.note_fr: 'What's driving it?' = qu'est-ce qui l'explique ? Question fréquente en comité.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Not yet with any certainty. Both sites changed their shift patterns over the summer, and both have relatively new site managers. I'd rather not jump to conclusions, so I'm proposing a deep dive for the January meeting.
lines.note_fr: 'To jump to conclusions' = tirer des conclusions hâtives.

lines.speaker: Martin
lines.text: Fine. But I'd like more than a diagnosis - come back with options and what they'd cost.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Absolutely. I'll bring a costed set of options, and I'll talk to both site managers before then so there are no surprises.
lines.note_fr: 'Costed options' = options chiffrées. 'No surprises' : règle d'or du 'managing upwards'.

questions.q: Why is Fiona not worried about time to hire?
options: It has improved since last year
It is the expected result of the hiring freeze
It is below the industry average
questions.explain_fr: « That's the freeze doing what it's supposed to do » : c'est la conséquence voulue du gel.

questions.q: Why does Sophie reject the flu-season explanation?
options: The pattern of absences does not match it
questions.explain_fr: Absences courtes, surtout le lundi, commencées en septembre : « it doesn't quite fit ».

questions.q: What does Martin ask Sophie to bring in January?
options: A list of employees with high absence
Costed options, not only an analysis
A proposal to lift the hiring freeze
questions.explain_fr: « Come back with options and what they'd cost » : il veut des solutions chiffrées, pas seulement un diagnostic.

dialogues.title: 'I want him out today'
dialogues.context: Greg, an American operations director at the Paris office of Halden Systems, calls Sophie, the HR Director, minutes after an employee, Karim, swore at him in front of the team.
dialogues.context_fr: Greg, directeur des opérations américain du bureau parisien de Halden Systems, appelle Sophie, la DRH, quelques minutes après qu'un salarié, Karim, l'a insulté devant l'équipe.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Sophie, I need you to fire Karim. Today. He just cursed me out in front of the whole team, and I'm done.
lines.note_fr: 'To curse someone out' (US) = insulter quelqu'un copieusement. 'I'm done' = j'en ai assez.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Okay, Greg, I hear you. That sounds completely unacceptable. Before we talk about next steps, can you tell me exactly what happened and who was there?
lines.note_fr: 'I hear you' : on accueille l'émotion sans valider la demande. On recentre immédiatement sur les faits.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: I told him his release notes were late again, and he stood up and called me an incompetent idiot - and worse. Four or five people saw it.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Got it. So, here's the thing: in France you can't fire someone on the spot, even for something like this. There's a procedure, and if we skip it, the dismissal is challengeable no matter how bad the behavior was.
lines.note_fr: 'Here's the thing' : annonce directe, très américaine. 'On the spot' = sur-le-champ. 'Behavior' : orthographe US.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: You're kidding me. So he just comes back in tomorrow like nothing happened?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Not necessarily. If we think this could amount to serious misconduct, we can suspend him on full pay pending the outcome - that's a precautionary measure, not a sanction. It keeps him out of the office while we look into it.
lines.note_fr: La mise à pied conservatoire est expliquée simplement. 'Pending' = dans l'attente de.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Okay, that's something. Then what?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: We get written accounts from the people who were there, today or tomorrow while it's fresh. Then we send him a letter inviting him to a meeting, he gets to give his side, and only after that do we decide. Realistically, we're looking at two to three weeks.
lines.note_fr: Rappel de la procédure en termes simples : convocation, entretien préalable, décision. 'While it's fresh' = tant que c'est frais dans les mémoires.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Three weeks. Back home this would've been a ten-minute conversation.
lines.note_fr: Allusion à l'emploi 'at-will' américain.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: I know it's frustrating. But a knee-jerk firing could cost us far more than three weeks if he takes it to the labor court. And one more thing - is there any background here? Has anything like this happened before, or has he raised any concerns himself?
lines.note_fr: 'Knee-jerk' = réflexe, irréfléchi. Question clé : vérifier qu'il n'y a pas un contexte (plainte, harcèlement) qui changerait l'analyse.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Not that I know of. He's been touchy since the reorg, but nothing like this.
lines.note_fr: 'Touchy' = susceptible, à cran. 'Reorg' = abréviation familière de 'reorganization'.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Okay. Don't say anything more to him for now. I'll call our employment lawyer and get back to you within the hour with the suspension letter.
lines.note_fr: Consigne claire au manager et délai précis : on reprend la main sans le désavouer.

questions.q: What can the company do immediately, according to Sophie?
options: Cut his pay for the day
Suspend him on full pay while the facts are examined
questions.explain_fr: La mise à pied conservatoire (« suspend him on full pay pending the outcome ») permet de l'écarter sans préjuger de la sanction.

questions.q: Why does Sophie want written accounts quickly?
options: The law requires them within 24 hours
Witnesses remember events better soon afterwards
questions.explain_fr: « While it's fresh » : les témoignages sont plus précis à chaud.

questions.q: Why does Sophie ask about the background?
options: To check for context that could change the analysis
questions.explain_fr: Un antécédent ou une alerte du salarié (harcèlement, conflit) pourrait modifier le risque juridique : il faut le savoir avant d'agir.

dialogues.title: A call with a US VP about culture
dialogues.context: Karen, VP People at Halden Systems in Chicago, wants to roll out the group's 'Speak Up, Move Fast' culture program to the French subsidiary. She is on a video call with Sophie.
dialogues.context_fr: Karen, VP People de Halden Systems à Chicago, veut déployer dans la filiale française le programme culturel du groupe « Speak Up, Move Fast ». Elle est en visioconférence avec Sophie.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: So, Sophie, the big ask from leadership is that every site lives the values by Q2. How do you think 'Speak Up, Move Fast' will land in Paris?
lines.note_fr: 'The big ask' = la grande demande. 'How will it land?' = comment sera-t-il reçu ?

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Honestly? 'Move fast' will land well with the engineers. 'Speak up' is where I'd be careful - not because people don't have opinions, believe me, but because of how they share them.
lines.note_fr: On commence par le positif, puis on nuance. 'Believe me' ajoute une touche d'humour.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: Say more.
lines.note_fr: 'Say more' : formule américaine très directe pour inviter à développer.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: In a lot of French teams, people will challenge an idea openly in a meeting, sometimes quite bluntly. But they're much less comfortable giving a manager personal feedback, especially in writing. It can feel like a breach of the hierarchy.
lines.note_fr: Explication interculturelle factuelle, sans caricature.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: Interesting. Our playbook includes a monthly upward feedback survey, with names attached. Is that a problem?
lines.note_fr: 'Playbook' = guide de méthodes (image du football américain). 'Upward feedback' = feedback du collaborateur vers le manager.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Potentially, yes, on two levels. Culturally, named feedback on your boss will get very cautious answers. And legally, a new tool that collects data about employees and their managers would need to go to the works council first, and we'd have to look at the data protection side.
lines.note_fr: Deux niveaux distincts, culturel et juridique. La consultation du CSE et le RGPD sont évoqués sans jargon.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: Okay, that's helpful to know before we hit send. What would you suggest?
lines.note_fr: 'Before we hit send' = avant de lancer (image de l'e-mail).

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: I'd pilot it with two volunteer teams, make the survey anonymous, and have the managers themselves present the values - not HR. If the leaders here don't own it, it'll look like another program from head office.
lines.note_fr: 'To pilot' = tester en phase pilote. 'Own it' = se l'approprier. 'Program' : orthographe US.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: I like that. My only concern is timing - leadership wants consistency across all sites.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: I understand. I'd frame it as the same values, adapted delivery. We'd still report on the same metrics as everyone else, so you'd have the consistency where it matters.
lines.note_fr: Formule synthétique qui concilie cohérence groupe et adaptation locale.

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.text: Same values, adapted delivery - I can sell that. Can you put a one-pager together for me by Friday?
lines.note_fr: 'I can sell that' = je peux le défendre en interne. 'One-pager' = note d'une page.

lines.speaker: Sophie
lines.text: Sure. I'll include the works council timeline so nobody's caught off guard.
lines.note_fr: 'Caught off guard' = pris au dépourvu.

questions.q: What part of the program does Sophie think needs care?
options: Speaking up, especially giving managers personal feedback
questions.explain_fr: Elle anticipe une réticence à donner un feedback nominatif à son manager, surtout par écrit.

questions.q: Which legal point does Sophie raise?
options: Employees must be paid to answer
A new tool collecting employee data needs works council involvement and a data protection review
Values must be written in French
questions.explain_fr: Un nouvel outil de collecte de données sur les salariés implique en principe l'information-consultation du CSE et une analyse RGPD.

questions.q: How does Sophie reconcile group consistency and local adaptation?
options: Same values and metrics, but adapted delivery
Delaying the program by a year
questions.explain_fr: « Same values, adapted delivery » : mêmes valeurs et indicateurs, déploiement adapté.

roleplays.title: Advising a manager who has lost trust in a remote employee
roleplays.situation: Nathalie, a finance manager, wants to stop one of her analysts, Élodie, from working from home because she 'never knows what she's doing'. Élodie's work is delivered on time. Advise Nathalie.
roleplays.situation_fr: Nathalie, responsable financière, veut retirer le télétravail à une analyste, Élodie, car elle « ne sait jamais ce qu'elle fait ». Le travail d'Élodie est rendu dans les délais. Conseillez Nathalie.

turns.say: I want Élodie back in the office five days a week. When she's at home, I have no idea what she's doing.
turns.model: I can see why that's frustrating. Can I ask what prompted this now? Has something gone wrong with her work, or is it more a feeling that you've lost visibility?
turns.tips_fr: Accueillez la frustration, puis posez une question ouverte pour distinguer un problème réel d'une impression.

turns.say: Her work's fine, actually. It's just that she doesn't always answer straight away on Teams.
turns.model: So the output is fine, and the issue is really about availability. That's a fair thing to want, but it's a different problem, and it's one you can fix by setting clear expectations - for example, agreeing core hours when she needs to be reachable.
turns.tips_fr: Reformulez pour recadrer : 'So the output is fine'. Distinguez résultat et disponibilité.

turns.say: Can't I just tell her remote working's over for her?
turns.model: I'd advise against that. If remote working is provided for in our agreement or charter, withdrawing it from one person without an objective reason could look like a sanction in disguise, and it would expose us. More importantly, you'd risk losing a good analyst over something a conversation could solve.
turns.tips_fr: 'I'd advise against that' : conseil ferme mais poli. Donnez le risque juridique en termes généraux, puis l'argument managérial.

turns.say: Fine. So what do I actually say to her?
turns.model: I'd keep it simple and positive. Start by saying her work is good. Then explain that you need to be able to reach her during certain hours and ask what would work for her. Agree it together, and follow up with a short email so you're both clear.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez une trame concrète en trois étapes. Terminez par la trace écrite.

turns.say: And if it doesn't improve?
turns.model: Then come back to me and we'll look at the next step together. But in my experience, once expectations are clear, most of these issues sort themselves out.
turns.tips_fr: Rassurez sur le soutien RH ('we'll look at it together') et terminez sur une note optimiste mais réaliste.

roleplays.title: Presenting the HR roadmap to the executive committee
roleplays.situation: You are presenting the 2027 HR roadmap to the executive committee of Corvane Logistics France. Fiona, the CFO, is sceptical about the cost and challenges you.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous présentez la feuille de route RH 2027 au comité exécutif de Corvane Logistics France. Fiona, directrice financière, est sceptique sur le coût et vous challenge.

turns.say: Before you start, Sophie - we have ten minutes. What do you need from us today?
turns.model: Thank you, I'll be brief. I'm asking the committee to approve the 2027 HR roadmap and a budget of six hundred and twenty thousand euros. Let me walk you through the three priorities and why they matter to the business plan.
turns.tips_fr: Commencez par la décision attendue (BLUF). Annoncez le plan en une phrase.

turns.say: Six hundred thousand is a lot of money for training. What's the return?
turns.model: It's a fair question. Most of the budget is funded by savings on agency fees: absence and turnover are costing us the equivalent of around twelve full-time posts in temporary cover. If we bring regretted attrition down to below nine per cent, the programme largely pays for itself within two years.
turns.tips_fr: Validez la question ('It's a fair question'), puis répondez en chiffres et en langage financier : coût évité, retour sur investissement.

turns.say: Can't the managers just learn on the job, like we all did?
turns.model: Some do, but the data suggests many don't. Half of our frontline managers have been in post for less than two years, and the sites with the newest managers are exactly where absence is rising. I'd rather invest now than keep paying for it in cover costs.
turns.tips_fr: Ne contestez pas l'expérience de votre interlocutrice ; opposez des données factuelles. 'I'd rather... than...' exprime une préférence argumentée.

turns.say: What's the biggest risk?
turns.model: Honestly, implementation. If site directors don't free up their managers' time, attendance will drop. That's why I'm asking for manager capability to be included in the directors' objectives - so it's owned by the business, not just by HR.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaître un risque renforce la crédibilité. Proposez immédiatement la parade.

turns.say: All right. If we approve it, how will we know it's working?
turns.model: You'll see it in the quarterly dashboard: regretted attrition, short-term absence and the share of managers trained, each against a target. I'll flag early if we're off track rather than wait for the year-end review.
turns.tips_fr: Concluez avec des indicateurs précis et un engagement de transparence ('I'll flag early').

roleplays.title: Challenging a CEO tactfully
roleplays.situation: Rajiv Menon, CEO of the French subsidiary of an Indian group, wants to cancel the manager training programme mid-year to save costs. You believe this is a mistake. Challenge him tactfully and propose an alternative.
roleplays.situation_fr: Rajiv Menon, CEO de la filiale française d'un groupe indien, veut annuler en cours d'année le programme de formation des managers pour faire des économies. Vous pensez que c'est une erreur. Contestez la décision avec tact et proposez une alternative.

turns.say: Sophie, we're behind on margin. I've decided to stop the manager programme for the rest of the year. I assume that's not a problem.
turns.model: I understand the pressure on margin, and I'm happy to look at savings in HR. Before we stop the programme, though, could I take five minutes to share what we'd be giving up? I think it affects the cost picture.
turns.tips_fr: Ne dites pas non d'emblée. Montrez que vous partagez l'objectif, puis demandez un temps d'écoute précis.

turns.say: Go on, but the decision is more or less made.
turns.model: Of course. Two-thirds of the budget has already been committed, so stopping now saves relatively little. And the first cohort is the sites with the highest absence. If we pull the programme there, we risk losing the improvement we're starting to see.
turns.tips_fr: Avancez des faits qui changent l'équation financière. Restez sur le terrain du dirigeant : coûts, résultats.

turns.say: You HR people always defend training. Give me something concrete.
turns.model: Fair challenge. At the Lyon site, short-term absence has dropped by a point since the managers there were trained. At current cover rates, that's worth more than the remaining budget for the whole programme. I can send you the figures this afternoon.
turns.tips_fr: Ne vous justifiez pas sur le reproche ; répondez avec un chiffre et proposez de l'étayer par écrit.

turns.say: Hmm. So what do you suggest?
turns.model: A middle way: we keep the programme at the two priority sites, postpone the other sites to next year, and switch part of the content to online modules. That would save around forty per cent of the remaining spend without losing the momentum where it matters most.
turns.tips_fr: Proposez un compromis chiffré : le dirigeant garde sa décision d'économie, vous protégez l'essentiel.

turns.say: And if I still say no?
turns.model: Then it's your call, and I'll make it work. I'd just ask that we note the risk on absence, so we can look at it again in the next quarterly review.
turns.tips_fr: Respectez l'autorité du CEO ('it's your call') tout en laissant une trace de votre conseil. C'est la marque du 'trusted adviser'.

roleplays.title: Handling a manager's complaint about HR
roleplays.situation: Paul, a site director, storms into your office: HR is 'slow and blocks everything', he has been waiting three weeks for approval to replace a departing technician. Handle his complaint.
roleplays.situation_fr: Paul, directeur de site, débarque dans votre bureau : les RH sont « lentes et bloquent tout » ; il attend depuis trois semaines l'accord pour remplacer un technicien démissionnaire. Gérez sa plainte.

turns.say: Honestly, HR is a brick wall. Three weeks to replace one technician! Do you have any idea what that's doing to my site?
turns.model: Three weeks is too long, and I'm sorry it's put your site under pressure. Let me find out exactly where it's stuck. Can you tell me when you submitted the request and who you've been dealing with?
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez le problème sans vous défendre. Passez vite aux faits ('where it's stuck').

turns.say: I sent it to your team on the 2nd. Nobody's come back to me.
turns.model: That's not acceptable - you should at least have had an answer. From what I can see, the request is waiting for the CFO's sign-off because of the hiring freeze. That's not an excuse, but it explains part of the delay.
turns.tips_fr: Distinguez la faute RH (pas de réponse) de la contrainte de gouvernance (gel des embauches). Assumez la première.

turns.say: So it's finance blocking it, not you?
turns.model: It's a process we all agreed to, so I don't want to pass the buck. What I can do is put the business case to the CFO today myself. As this is a maintenance role, it should qualify as business-critical.
turns.tips_fr: 'I don't want to pass the buck' : évitez de rejeter la faute. Proposez une action concrète et immédiate.

turns.say: Fine. But this keeps happening. Why does everything take so long?
turns.model: You're right that it's a pattern, and that's something we need to fix. Part of the problem is that every request goes through the same queue, whatever its urgency. I'd like to agree a fast track for critical roles at your site - would you be willing to give me your list of critical roles this week?
turns.tips_fr: Transformez la plainte en amélioration du processus et impliquez le manager dans la solution.

turns.say: All right. I'll send it tomorrow.
turns.model: Thank you. I'll come back to you by tomorrow evening on the technician, either way. And thanks for raising it directly - I'd much rather hear it from you than through the grapevine.
turns.tips_fr: Engagement daté, quelle que soit la réponse. 'Through the grapevine' = par la rumeur : on valorise la franchise.
